chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Muḥammad ibn Shuʿayb, from Abī Kahmas, who said:

I was present at the death of Ismāʿīl عليه السلام while Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was sitting beside him. When death came upon him, he bound his jaws, closed his eyes, and covered him with the blanket. Then he ordered that he be prepared, and when he had finished with his matter, he called for his shroud and wrote on the edge of the shroud:
“Ismāʿīl bears witness that there is no god but Allah.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: He is to be turbaned as a living person is turbaned, and his jaw is to be bound with the turban, and its two ends are to be placed upon his chest. Its explanation has already passed, and this also clarifies it.

key_terms.بِتَهْيِئَتِهِ: his preparation; the arrangements made for the deceased
key_terms.صَدْرِهِ: his chest; where the two ends of the turban are placed
key_terms.كَفَنِهِ: his shroud; the cloth used for burial
key_terms.لَحْيَيْهِ: his jaws; referring to binding the mouth closed after death
key_terms.ٱلْعِمَامَةِ: the turban used in the burial preparation
key_terms.ٱلْمَوْتُ: death; the moment of passing away
key_terms.ٱلْمِلْحَفَةَ: the blanket or covering placed over the deceased

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām narrate about preparing the deceased and writing the shahadah on the shroud?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the final moments and post-death preparation of Ismāʿīl عليه السلام in the presence of Imam Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام. It records practical rites for the deceased, including closing the eyes, binding the jaw, covering the body, preparing the shroud, and writing the shahadah upon it, with an additional note from al-Shaykh on how the turban is to be arranged.
